Box B-3 defines substantial (several supportive findings from good-quality studies, very few or no credible opposing findings), moderate (several from good- to fair-quality studies, very few or no credible opposing findings; limitations including chance, bias and confounding cannot be ruled out with reasonable confidence), limited (fair-quality studies or mixed findings with most favouring one conclusion; significant uncertainty) and no or insufficient (mixed findings, a single poor study, or not studied). Primary studies were reviewed guided by the Cochrane tool for randomised trials and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort and case-control studies. The report says the committee was not tasked to conduct a systematic review and that literature may have been missed. Method, wording of conclusions: evidence was privileged in the order randomised trials, non-randomised controlled trials, prospective controlled studies, case-control studies, with case series only when nothing better. The weight of evidence was decided in private deliberations of committee subgroups. Box B-3 defines substantial (several supportive findings from good-quality studies, very few or no credible opposing findings), moderate (several supportive findings from good- to fair-quality studies, very few or no credible opposing findings; limitations including chance, bias and confounding cannot be ruled out with reasonable confidence), limited (fair-quality studies or mixed findings with most favouring one conclusion; significant uncertainty) and no or insufficient (mixed findings, a single poor study, or not studied).
